findings.title: A view-all-groups permission grants permission to create groups
findings.body: `canManage()` is used by `POST /groups` to authorize top-level group creation, but it evaluates both the `view` and `manage` scopes. Consequently, an administrator granted only the read-only all-groups `view` scope can create arbitrary top-level groups. This is a write privilege escalation; `canManage()` should require only the `manage` scope, matching the per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` behavior.

findings.title: Individual group authorization resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: When a permission references an individual group, this method creates its authorization resource and scopes but never calls `resource.setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` enumerates resources using `findByType(..., "Groups", ...)`, so these untyped individual resources are omitted. As a result, a delegate with `view-members` or `manage-members` on a specific group cannot have that group's members included in user searches or counts. Set the resource type when creating schema-managed resources.

findings.title: User filtering uses authorization resource IDs instead of realm group IDs
findings.body: The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission` and adds that same value to the returned set. This ID is the authorization-store resource ID, whereas the resource name is the realm `GroupModel` ID established by `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`. `hasPermission` subsequently looks up a resource by name, so it misses the individual resource and falls back to the all-groups resource; moreover, `UserModel.GROUPS` and the user-count overload expect realm group IDs, not authorization resource IDs. Specific group member permissions therefore produce invalid query filters and users/counts are incorrectly empty or otherwise incorrect. Evaluate and return `groupResource.getName()` after ensuring it represents a group resource.

findings.title: Existing enabled admin-permissions realms are never upgraded with Groups scopes and resource
findings.body: `init` returns immediately whenever an admin-permissions client already exists. The new `Groups` all-resource and its scopes are only created later in this method, so realms that enabled V2 before this version retain no `Groups`, `manage-membership`, `manage-members`, or `view-members` records. Creating a group scope permission in such a realm fails scope validation because the scope does not exist, and group authorization checks cannot resolve their all-groups resource. Add an idempotent schema upgrade path for existing admin-permissions clients rather than only bootstrapping new clients.

findings.title: V2-only deployments no longer clean up authorization resources for deleted groups
findings.body: V2 evaluators are selected by `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, but the provider event listener is now registered only when the separate V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is enabled. In a V2-only configuration, `GroupRemovedEvent` has no handler, so group-specific authorization resources and their policies created for the new Groups type remain after the realm group is deleted. These orphaned records accumulate and remain visible/usable through the authorization store. Register a V2-aware cleanup handler (without calling the V1-only `setPermissionsEnabled` implementation) whenever V2 is enabled.
